title: LLM-Powered Code Analysis and Optimization for Gaussian Splatting Kernels

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-assisted profiling-guided correctness-preserving optimization of CUDA Gaussian-splatting rendering kernels
mechanism.populationDetail: The paper uses the OpenEvolve evolutionary-search framework but does not describe the maintained population organization, island structure, or genealogy.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The paper mentions quality-diversity evaluation and tracking the best candidate, but does not specify a separate archive structure, descriptor cells, or elite preservation rule.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Evolution runs over candidates in OpenEvolve and records the best candidate over iterations, but offspring insertion and survivor replacement are not described.
mechanism.generationDetail: The prompt explicitly restricts edits to the marked EVOLVE-BLOCK in one provided source program and asks for the full code with markers preserved.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The combined scalar score is based on accuracy and latency; Nsight system/workload profiling is provided to the planner to prune suggestions. GPT-5 also supplies a functional-equivalence check for generated code.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The example prompt contains one program with an editable EVOLVE-BLOCK, but the paper does not specify how OpenEvolve samples that parent from its search state.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/LLM-Powered Code Analysis and Optimization for Gaussian Splatting Kernels.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently cites this paper in application.tex. OpenEvolve population/archive/replacement details are not reported in this paper and should not be inferred from the framework. Distinguish GPT-5 planning/checking plus Deepseek evolutionary generation from separate one-shot model comparisons; profiler data is external metadata reused to prune search guidance.
